rules.title: Coroutine launched in GlobalScope
rules.description: Work launched in `GlobalScope` escapes every lifecycle and cannot be cancelled. Use a scope tied to the component, or one supplied by the caller.

rules.title: AsyncTask used
rules.description: `AsyncTask` is deprecated and leaks the enclosing instance. Use coroutines or an executor.

rules.title: runBlocking in production code
rules.description: `runBlocking` blocks the caller's thread; on the main thread it freezes the UI and can cause an ANR. Test code is not checked.

rules.title: Dispatcher hard-coded
rules.description: Dispatchers are injected, not named in the code, so the code stays testable.

rules.title: Blocking work on the main thread
rules.description: No I/O, disk access or heavy computation on the main thread; move it off with `withContext(Dispatchers.IO)` or the equivalent.

rules.title: Coroutine launched outside a lifecycle scope
rules.description: Every coroutine starts from a scope tied to a lifecycle (`viewModelScope`, a UI scope, or one supplied by the caller). No free-floating jobs.

rules.title: async awaited at once
rules.description: Use `async`/`await` for work that is really concurrent. A single `async` awaited at once is a `suspend` call with extra machinery; use `coroutineScope` or `supervisorScope` to decompose in parallel.

rules.title: Flow errors not handled
rules.description: Errors of a stream are handled with `catch`: a failing flow must not stop emitting silently.

rules.title: Cold flow without flowOn
rules.description: A cold flow that does I/O declares its context with `flowOn` instead of relying on the collector's.

rules.title: Mutable flow exposed
rules.description: `MutableStateFlow` and `MutableSharedFlow` stay private and are exposed with `asStateFlow()` or `asSharedFlow()`. A caller that can emit into your state makes the owner's invariants unenforceable.

rules.title: Mutable collection in a public API
rules.description: A public API exposes `List`, `Map` and `Set`, not their mutable counterparts.

rules.title: Screen state not modelled
rules.description: Screen state is a sealed hierarchy or an immutable data class, not a handful of independent booleans that can contradict each other.

rules.title: One-shot event in the state
rules.description: One-shot events (navigation, snackbar, dialog) have their own stream. In the state object, a re-emission would replay them.

rules.title: LiveData in new code
rules.description: No `LiveData`, `MutableLiveData` or `MediatorLiveData` in new or changed code: use `StateFlow` or `SharedFlow`. Allowed only with a comment on the declaration that justifies it.

rules.title: Broadcast used inside the process
rules.description: No `LocalBroadcastManager`, and no `BroadcastReceiver` for communication inside the process: use a Flow or a Channel. A receiver for system broadcasts is allowed with a comment that justifies it.

rules.title: Empty catch block
rules.description: An error that vanishes is a bug that will be diagnosed twice. A `catch` block holds at least a handling statement or a comment that explains why the error is ignored.

rules.title: Generic exception caught
rules.description: Catch specific exceptions, not `Exception` or `Throwable`, unless the boundary really handles everything.

rules.title: Failure logged and dropped
rules.description: Failures reach the caller or the UI, as `Resource<T>` or the error type the module declares. They are never logged and dropped.

rules.title: Not-null assertion
rules.description: BLOCKER when the value comes from outside the process or the user (network, deserialization, IPC, deep link, intent extras, platform callback, user input); MAJOR otherwise. In existing code the BLOCKER case needs a verified crash path, otherwise it is MAJOR. Resolve nullability with `?.`, `?:`, `requireNotNull` with a message, or a smart cast. Known exception: the ViewBinding accessor `get() = _binding!!` is never reported.

rules.title: Hand-written precondition
rules.description: Use `require`, `check` or `error` for preconditions and invariants instead of `if (...) throw ...`.

rules.title: Field injection
rules.description: Constructor injection over field injection: it makes the dependency explicit and the class testable. Fields injected in a Hilt entry point class are allowed.

rules.title: Dependency built by hand
rules.description: No direct construction of what the graph provides: it bypasses scoping and cannot be replaced in tests.

rules.title: DI annotation missing
rules.description: ViewModels and injection entry points carry the annotations Hilt requires: `@HiltViewModel` on ViewModels, `@AndroidEntryPoint` on Fragments and Activities, `@Inject constructor` for injected classes.

rules.title: Binding provided twice
rules.description: No second module provides a binding that already exists, and modules live where the project keeps them.

rules.title: Static accessor as a hidden dependency
rules.description: No static or global accessor used as a hidden dependency.

rules.title: var never reassigned
rules.description: `val` by default; `var` only where the value really changes.

rules.title: Collection built by mutation
rules.description: Build collections with `listOf`, `mapOf` or `buildList` rather than creating a mutable one and filling it, unless mutation is needed.

rules.title: Data holder is not a data class
rules.description: Pure data holders are `data class`.

rules.title: Identifier passed as a raw type
rules.description: A single-value identifier or token that crosses a boundary is a `@JvmInline value class`, so two `String` ids cannot be swapped by accident.

rules.title: Hand-rolled loop
rules.description: Collection operators (`map`, `filter`, `firstOrNull`, `associateBy`, `sumOf`) instead of hand-rolled loops.

rules.title: Standard library reimplemented
rules.description: Use the standard library (`runCatching`, `buildList`, `takeIf`, `groupBy` and friends) instead of reimplementing it.

rules.title: Large pipeline not lazy
rules.description: Use `asSequence()` for large or multi-step pipelines.

rules.title: when with else over a closed type
rules.description: A `when` over a sealed type or an enum has no `else`, so a new case fails to compile until every use handles it.

rules.title: Long if/else-if chain
rules.description: Use `when` instead of a long `if / else if` chain.

rules.title: Unsafe cast
rules.description: Prefer `is` smart casts to `as`; use `as?` where a cast can fail legitimately.

rules.title: Indexing that can throw
rules.description: Prefer `firstOrNull` and `getOrNull` to indexing that can throw.

rules.title: Boolean flag parameter
rules.description: No positional boolean flag that switches behaviour: use named arguments with defaults, or two functions. At the call site `doThing(true)` says nothing.

rules.title: Block body for one expression
rules.description: A function of a single expression has an expression body.

rules.title: Redundant type annotation
rules.description: Let the compiler infer local types. Annotate explicitly on public or overridable signatures, where the type is part of the contract.

rules.title: Utils holder instead of extension
rules.description: Write an extension function rather than another member of a static-style `Utils` holder.

rules.title: Scope functions nested
rules.description: One purpose per scope function (`let` for a non-null value, `apply` to configure, `also` for side effects, `run` or `with` to produce a result), and no nesting that hurts readability.

rules.title: Java in new code
rules.description: New code is Kotlin, unless it changes an area that is deliberately Java-only.

rules.title: Refactoring outside the ticket
rules.description: The change does what the ticket says. A broad rewrite of untouched code by the author hides the real change in noise. It applies only to refactoring done by the author, never to reporting existing defects.

rules.title: Business logic in the wrong layer
rules.description: Business logic sits in the domain or presentation layer, not in mappers or data sources. UI classes have more specific rules in the Views and Compose checklists.

rules.title: Class with more than one responsibility
rules.description: One responsibility per class: a class that needs "and" to be described is the finding.

rules.title: Long function
rules.description: Functions are short and single-purpose.

rules.title: Deep nesting
rules.description: Nesting is shallow: prefer early returns to another level of `if`.

rules.title: Logic duplicated across classes
rules.description: Logic repeated across two or more classes is centralised once. Repetition inside one class is not this rule.

rules.title: Line too long
rules.description: Lines stay within 100 characters. Only lines the change adds are reported.

rules.title: Package structure not followed
rules.description: New code follows the package structure of the project; prefer grouping by feature to a technical dumping ground.

rules.title: Context retained beyond its lifecycle
rules.description: No `Activity`, `Fragment` or view `Context` is retained beyond its lifecycle: not in a long-lived object, a companion or a static field. Adapters and composables have more specific rules.

rules.title: Context in a ViewModel
rules.description: No `Context` in a ViewModel unless it is needed and a comment says why: it outlives configuration changes.

rules.title: Listener never removed
rules.description: Every registered listener, observer, callback or receiver is removed on the matching teardown.

rules.title: Unnecessary WeakReference
rules.description: `WeakReference` only where the lifetime really needs it: used to paper over a leak it hides the real ownership problem.

rules.title: Bitmap in a model
rules.description: No `Bitmap` inside a domain or data model.

rules.title: Whole list refreshed
rules.description: Lists use `DiffUtil` or Paging, not a full refresh (`notifyDataSetChanged`) on every change.

rules.title: Strict dependency version
rules.description: No strict version on any dependency: the `!!` suffix (`"group:name:1.2.3!!"`), `version { strictly(...) }` in a build script, or `{ strictly = "..." }` in a version catalog. A strict version overrides every other request for that module in the whole build; another module asking for a different version is silently forced to this one, or the build fails to resolve. Declare the plain version. A `-SNAPSHOT` version is allowed.

rules.title: Dependency version changed
rules.description: No dependency version change inside a feature branch without prior agreement: it affects every module and, in a library, every consumer, and it is invisible in a diff that is about something else.

rules.title: New third-party dependency
rules.description: A new third-party dependency needs prior agreement. In a library every consumer inherits it. Using `kapt` instead of KSP is a known exception and is never reported.

rules.title: Shared library imports another
rules.description: No shared library imports another shared library without agreement: it multiplies the coupling every consumer inherits.

rules.title: Naming convention broken
rules.description: `PascalCase` for types, `camelCase` for functions and properties, `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE` for constants.

rules.title: Name does not say what it is
rules.description: Names say what the thing is, in English.

rules.title: Declaration without KDoc
rules.description: MAJOR on a public symbol of a library (profile library) or of a module other modules call; MINOR otherwise. Public types, public functions and non-obvious properties are documented. In a library the documentation states preconditions, threading and what it throws: consumers read the documentation, not the source.

rules.title: Comment that adds nothing
rules.description: Inline comments only where the logic is not obvious.

rules.title: Secret in the source
rules.description: No credentials, API keys, tokens or environment URLs in the source: they come from build configuration or a secure store.

rules.title: Sensitive data logged
rules.description: No logging of credentials, session tokens, personal data or payment payloads.

rules.title: External input not validated
rules.description: Data that crosses a trust boundary (network, IPC, deep link, WebView bridge, the public entry point of a library) is validated before use.

rules.title: WebView bridge exposes too much
rules.description: A JavaScript bridge exposes the minimum surface, never arbitrary execution or sensitive data, and validates everything that arrives from the page.

rules.title: Sensitive value in plain storage
rules.description: Sensitive values are not written to plain preferences or files.

rules.title: Missing unit tests
rules.description: Unit tests for every ViewModel, repository, mapper or helper added or changed and, in a library, for every public entry point added or changed. It is checked on the whole change request, not on one file.

rules.title: Empty test stub
rules.description: No scaffolded test is left empty: it reports green while covering nothing.

rules.title: Test name says nothing
rules.description: The name of a test states what is tested and the expected outcome, as in `shouldReturnX_whenY()`.

rules.title: Test without assertions
rules.description: Every test asserts on a result, not only that no exception was thrown.

rules.title: Binding kept after the view is destroyed
rules.description: A Fragment releases its binding in `onDestroyView()`. The view hierarchy is destroyed while the Fragment instance survives; a retained binding leaks the whole view tree. XML layouts with ViewBinding instead of Jetpack Compose are accepted and never reported.

rules.title: lateinit binding
rules.description: No `lateinit` for a binding or any property tied to the view lifecycle: it stays a stale non-null reference after teardown. Use a nullable backing field or `by lazy`.

rules.title: findViewById where binding is available
rules.description: No `findViewById` where binding is available: it is unchecked at compile time and queries the hierarchy again.

rules.title: Binding used after onDestroyView
rules.description: No access to the binding from a callback that can fire after `onDestroyView`: a network result, a timer, a flow collected on the wrong scope.

rules.title: launchWhenStarted used
rules.description: Collect with `viewLifecycleOwner.lifecycleScope.launch { repeatOnLifecycle(Lifecycle.State.STARTED) { ... } }`, never `launchWhenStarted`: it suspends the coroutine but keeps the collection alive, so upstream work goes on and the observer stays attached to a destroyed view.

rules.title: Fragment owner used for UI observation
rules.description: In a Fragment, UI collection and observation use `viewLifecycleOwner`, not `this`. The Fragment outlives its view, so the wrong owner leaks across view recreation.

rules.title: Wiring in onCreateView
rules.description: `onCreateView` inflates; wiring belongs in `onViewCreated`.

rules.title: Business logic in a UI class
rules.description: No business logic in `Fragment`, `Activity`, `Service` or adapters: it cannot be unit tested, and it is a non-negotiable team rule.

rules.title: Adapter holds a Context
rules.description: An adapter or ViewHolder does not retain an `Activity` or a listener beyond the life of the view.

rules.title: Deep view hierarchy
rules.description: Avoid nesting layouts where a constraint-based layout would be flat: depth costs on every measure pass.

rules.title: Literal in a layout
rules.description: Dimensions, colours and strings come from resources, not from literals in the layout or in the code.

rules.title: View without content description
rules.description: Meaningful views carry a content description; decorative ones are explicitly excluded.
